name: Freelance academic editor / proofreader
summary: Edit and proofread students' academic papers for Scribbr at fixed per-word rates; requires native-level English and a university degree.
whatYouDo: You claim editing orders (theses, essays, papers), correct language and comment on structure and clarity within a set deadline. Rates are fixed per word and higher for shorter deadlines.
appeal: Structured entry into paid editing with set per-word rates
Scribbr states average earnings of roughly €20–30 per hour
Onboarding training through the Scribbr Academy
Remote; choose orders around your schedule
watchOuts: Bachelor's degree or higher and native English required
Multi-stage screening: 10-question language quiz (80+ to pass), test assignment, Academy training and 2–5 simulation orders; pay status of later stages unclear
Must be able to edit at least 10,000 words per week
Reviews describe a very hard entry barrier and actual hourly pay often below the advertised average
Hiring is periodic; applications are not always open
Rates are in euros; Canadian residency rules not stated on pages found

training.notes: Scribbr Academy training and simulation orders are part of onboarding; whether these stages are paid could not be confirmed.

compensation.notes: Scribbr FAQ: average approx. €20–30 per hour (EUR), based on fixed per-word rates that rise for shorter deadlines. Not recorded numerically because the currency is EUR. Reviews say real hourly earnings are often lower.

reliability.notes: Work depends on order volume; reviews mention periodic hiring.

applicationSteps: Take the 10-question language quiz (score 80+ to continue)
Create an account and upload CV, motivation letter and ID
Complete Scribbr Academy training and 2–5 simulation orders
fitsIf: You hold a degree, write excellent English and want a structured way to start earning from editing.
notFitIf: You have no degree, or cannot commit to around 10,000 words of editing per week.

sources.title: How can I become a Scribbr editor?
sources.notes: Steps: language quiz, account with CV/motivation letter/ID, test assignment, Scribbr Academy, 2–5 simulation orders; native speakers and university degree required (per search summary of Scribbr pages).

sources.title: Scribbr language quiz
sources.notes: 10-question quiz; bachelor's degree or higher; able to edit at least 10,000 words per week; score of 80+ leads to the test assignment.

sources.title: How much will I earn as a Scribbr editor?
sources.notes: Average approx. €20–30 per hour based on fixed per-word rates; shorter deadlines pay more.

sources.title: Scribbr: A Platform for Freelance Editors and Proofreaders (with a super-hard entry barrier)
sources.notes: Review describing a very hard entry barrier. Search summaries of reviews also report pay below advertised and that Scribbr is not always accepting applications (not all pinned to this page).
